The Applicant requests amended Site Plan approval to revise the proposed development program to best serve the changing market. There are 3 primary areas and buildings that are subject of the proposed changes, minor development program changes, and zoning text amendments: Building F (Senior/Adult Living Building) Building F was approved in 2022 as an approximately 215,000 s/f building comprised of 90 age restricted Independent Living units and 110 Assisted Living/Memory Care units. Since approval, the Applicant has been actively marketing this portion of the site to developers and operators of age-restricted facilities in the region. The resounding response from the real estate market has been that the approved size and use mix does not meet the market demands and that development of this project component is not currently feasible. Nevertheless, the Applicant has identified a reputable development group, AMS Acquisitions, which has demonstrated a significant interest in the development of this site, subject to certain development program updates. The revised Building F development program includes eliminating the Assisted Living/Memory Care units (110 approved) and replacing same with 60 additional Independent Living units. This would bring the total Independent Living unit count to 150 units total. This would be accommodated through reducing the overall building height by 1 story (from 8 approved stories to 7 stories) and internal redesigns, as well as some minor updates to the building footprint to include more marketable lobby and amenity spaces. This update to the Building F programming will also be supported by the addition of 114 structure parking spaces at Building F. Jewel Box Building (Retail and Residential Amenity Building) The Jewel Box Building was approved as an approximately 24,000 s/f building supporting a mix of retail and residential amenity spaces. This building is located central to the Premises adjacent to the 0.50-acre open green space. The building was approved to include 14,200 s/f of residential amenity spaces and 9,800 s/f of retail space. Similar to Building F, the Applicant has been actively engaged with potential operators of the retail space within the Jewel Box Building. However, the Applicant has faced challenges obtaining interest in potential tenants for the approved retail space. Rather than risk the potential for longstanding vacancies at the heart of this development, the Applicant poses to redesign the interior building program of the Jewel Box to eliminate the retail space and provide more attractive residential amenity space. The Applicant therefore proposes to increase the total amenity space by 4,803 s/f, bringing the total amenity floor area space to 19,003 s/f, which would be contained within the same building footprint. The internal changes include eliminating a portion of the second floor amenity space to accommodate a new double-height first floor amenity gym/basketball court. The exchange of the approved retail space for amenity space would provide a more attractive residential product in a very competitive market and eliminate the likelihood of long-vacant commercial spaces. Building D (Multi-family Building) The approved Building D is a 261,223 s/f multi-family building supporting 331 residential units. As the Board is aware, the overall site development is governed by a project-wide Floor Area Ratio (FAR) cap of 0.8, which can be increased to 1.6 by the Applicant’s commitment to a $3,000,000 bonus payment. The Applicant has, and remains, committed to the $3,000,000 contribution. As a result of the Building F and Jewel Box changes and the other minor site-wide modifications, the total FAR as proposed would be below the permitted 1.6 FAR. To make up for this lost space elsewhere on the site, the Applicant is proposing to increase the Building D floor area by changing the building height from 6 stories to 7 stories (where 8 stories are permitted). This additional story would allow the Applicant to gain 52 additional units within Building D. As noted below, there is simultaneously proposed to be a reduction of 10 total units in Buildings B & C. Therefore, the total non-age restricted, residential unit count at the site is being increased from 957 to 999. However, when taking into consideration the reduction in the Assisted Living/Memory Care units, the total living units at the site are being reduced by 8 units. The change to the Building D development program is being supported by an additional 16 structured parking spaces, as well as the reduction in shared-parking needed with nearby uses due to the overall site reduction in commercial space. Minor development program changes: -Building A (Hotel Building): The proposal includes reducing the overall amenity space by 1,096 s/f and increasing the overall hotel unit floor area by 1,011 s/f. Importantly, this will not increase or decrease the total number of hotel units from the approved 120 units. There are no changes to the overall building footprint. - Building B (Mixed-Use Building): The proposal includes reducing the overall commercial/retail space by 1,459 s/f, adding 3,342 s/f of residential amenity space, and eliminating 7 total residential units. The total structured parking at this building will be reduced by 5 spaces. There are no changes to the overall building footprint. - Building C (Multi-family Building): The proposal includes the addition of 1,892 s/f of residential space (though this will actually result in the loss of 3 residential units) and the addition of 2,320 s/f of residential amenity space. The total structured parking at this building is being increased by 8 spaces. There are no changes to the overall building footprint. - Building E (Mixed Use Building): The proposal includes the addition of 117 s/f of commercial/retail space and a reduction of residential amenity space by 2,884 s/f. There are no changes to the overall building footprint. Petitioned Zoning Text Amendments: The SD-PMU District currently requires a minimum “Nonresidential” FAR of 25% across the entire Premises. As approved, the overall Site Plan complies with this requirement largely through the Assisted Living/Memory Care component which, by Village definition is not “Residential” due to the heightened level of service needed and the commercial nature of the operations. Similarly, the Jewel Box’s commercial/retail space adds to that “Nonresidential” FAR. By eliminating these components, the proposed changes to the overall site plan are resulting in the overall site redevelopment providing less than 25% Nonresidential FAR. The resulting “Nonresidential” FAR is approximately 8%. The Applicant is therefore petitioning that the Board of Trustees eliminate the 25% Nonresidential FAR requirement to accommodate the proposed site amendments. The Applicant submits its Petition for the Proposed Zoning Amendments which details the proposed request. As discussed more fully therein, the Proposed Zoning Amendments are consistent with the goals and objectives of the Village’s Comprehensive Plan. Specifically, the Proposed Zoning Amendments are proposed in furtherance of the redevelopment of the United Hospital site as a mixed-use development comprising of an appropriate mix of uses. The elimination of the Nonresidential FAR requirement will also support the Village’s goal of ensuring that the redevelopment does not adversely impact the Village Downtown’s retail and commercial base. These changes will actually accommodate a different demographic

The Project will consist of the installation of a new PFAS treatment building to house granular activated carbon (GAC) filtration vessels, which are to be used to reduce PFAS to regulatory compliance levels. The existing sodium hypochlorite and sodium hydroxide chemicals that feed the system will be relocated to dedicated rooms within the new building. An aboveground chlorine contact tank will be installed to replace the existing chamber. Additional process piping site improvements and associated modifications are required and further defined in the enclosed plans and engineer’s report. The Project will also include a paved driveway, an underground stormwater tank detection system, and an aboveground spill containment pad. By way of background, Veolia must undertake this project because it is required to comply with mandatory regulations from the US Environmental Protection Agency and NY State Department of Health concerning PFAS to provide potable water to its customers (the “Project”). The Applicant is seeking site plan approval to amend the Hudson Harbor Project with the final Phase 5 which is proposed to consist of approximately 102,000- sf, 4-story residential building with a total of 81 residential units and 1,500-sf of rooftop amenity space and 157 parking spaces. The site is approximately 2.12 acres and is located in the Waterfront General Business District (“WGBD”). The site is located at 0 Division Street and along Hudson View Way. It is Lot 9 in the Hudson Harbor development. It is currently improved with an unused parking lot, and is labeled as buildings “Q, R and S” in the Amended SEQRA Findings Statement dated June 19, 2006. The Property is part of the previously approved Hudson Harbor development and is the last phase (Phase 5) of that project which has not yet been completed. The original SEQRA Findings dated February 6, 2006 provided that “all roadways and sidewalks within the project site must be built to public road and sidewalk standards and dedicated to the Village as public roadways and sidewalks, unless an exemption is granted by the Planning Board during site plan review. The Applicant will be required to prepare a plan showing the roadways and sidewalks network within the project and their ability to meet these standards for dedication to the Village for review and final approval by the Planning Board. The original SEQRA Findings provided for a total of 871 parking spaces, which will not be impacted by the Phase 5 project. The Planning Board will require the specific location of all parking spaces on the Site to be finalized as part of the site plan approval process. The Applicant will cooperate with National Resources (the Master Developer) to close out the Hudson Harbor Project including the use of the Cooney Building and the Open Space Garden on the Cooney lot.

Rose Enterprises Group (“Applicant”), contract vendee of the property located at 235 Elm Road (“Property”), is seeking the following approvals from the Village of Briarcliff Manor Board of Trustees (“Board”): (i) establishment of a Downtown Adjacent Planned Unit Development (“DA-PUD”) District (§220-21.C) and (ii) Preliminary Planned Unit Development approval (“Preliminary PUD Approval”) pursuant to §220-21.C of the proposed draft legislation (“Proposed Action”). The Proposed Action would facilitate the development of the proposed Project, known as Renaissance Briarcliff Manor, which envisions the redevelopment of the vacant 37-acre former Pace University campus into a planned residential community. The proposed project includes 110 townhomes on the campus site and 5 single-family homes along Tuttle Road, complemented by permanent open space, including a publicly accessible walking trail system, landscaped buffers along Elm and Tuttle Roads and a 10-acre preserved wooded area, together encompassing approximately 30% of the Property. The proposed project also provides for residential amenities, including a clubhouse and pool.
